subject.title: Feature Request: Plugin Circuit Breaker for graceful degradation

question: What framework-level plugin circuit breaker contract should OpenClaw support for hook/tool execution, persistence, operator controls, and default degradation behavior?
rationale: Choosing fail modes, forced-open behavior, status/reset surfaces, storage schema, and default-on policy changes the plugin runtime and third-party plugin contract.

options.title: Design core breaker contract first
options.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, metrics/status/reset surfaces, default compatibility mode, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

options.title: Keep breakers plugin-owned
options.body: Continue with plugin-local breakers like Active Memory and add only narrow SDK helpers when multiple plugins prove the same need.

options.title: Start telemetry-only
options.body: Add attribution and passive log-only evaluation first, then decide active open/half-open behavior after deployment data.

recommendation.title: Design core breaker contract first
recommendation.body: Define the generic hook/tool breaker API, SQLite state schema, metrics/status/reset surfaces, default compatibility mode, and per-plugin degradation policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate across current hook, tool, lock, runtime-health, and Active Memory adjacent source history.
